clue.text: High layer backed skills to get odds here

indicators.note: backed means turned round, so the word for skills is read from its end

parts.note: arts are skills, as in the arts of war
taken as written
SP is starting price, the odds offered at the start of a race
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler is told to back skills at some upper level where good odds are on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ARTS into STRA. SP, the starting price, is the betting term for a horse's odds.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere's second layer sits above the weather, a high band of air above the troposphere.

clue.text: Yugoslavian archdeacon appears in plum outfit

indicators.note: appears in says the churchman's title shows up inside another word
the fruit word serves as an outfit, dressing round the title

parts.note: the sloe is a small wild plum
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A Yugoslav churchman turns up dressed in purple.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN, the abbreviated style of an archdeacon, goes inside SLOE. 'plum' looks like a colour, but it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Slovenia, once a republic of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: An awful resort — nothing sounds as foul!

indicators.note: an awful version is a mangled one, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: A complaint that a dreadful holiday spot sounds utterly foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges RESORT with O. 'sounds as foul' tells the solver to hear 'foul' as fowl, which a cock is.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a fowl, and the clue's word for it is spelt to sound alike.

clue.text: Financial officer to hold dear Rachel's capital

parts.note: to treasure something is to cherish it

indicators.note: capital means the capital, or first, letter of the name

explanation.surface: An accountant who treasures Rachel's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but takes R, the first letter of Rachel.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer in charge of a society's or company's funds keeps its accounts.

clue.text: Cuttlefish is very good in its natural habitat

indicators.note: in places the word for very good inside the word for the creature's home

parts.note: the cuttlefish lives in the sea
pi is crossword shorthand for pious, very good

explanation.surface: A cuttlefish is in fine health in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, goes inside SEA, the cuttlefish's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish's Latin genus name, also the brown ink it squirts.

clue.text: Jet hound

definitions.meaning: the British vertical take-off jump jet fighter
a dog bred for hunting hares

explanation.definitionFit: The name of both a jump-jet warplane and a hare-hunting dog breed.

clue.text: Managed old radio show in Burma

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a shop
The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy

explanation.surface: A vintage radio programme was produced in Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GOON SHOW was a classic British radio comedy with Spike Milligan and Peter Sellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The former capital city of Burma, now Myanmar, is a place in Burma.

clue.text: "May be equal" — heard in pantomime

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A line about equality is spoken during a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' looks like a homophone signal, and 'May' like a month, but 'May be' rearranges EQUAL HEARD IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic interlude in old English pantomime featuring the clown Harlequin.

clue.text: Habit of the huntin set

parts.note: the hunting fraternity famously clip the final letter from words like huntin', shootin' and fishin', and this clue names the grammatical term for that dropping of a word's last sound

explanation.surface: A remark on the customs of the fox-hunting gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like riding dress, but it means a speech habit, the dropped final G shown in the clue's own 'huntin''.
explanation.definitionFit: The linguistic term for cutting off the end of a word, as in huntin' for hunting.

clue.text: Standard cut vegetable

parts.note: par is a standard or norm, as in up to par
a snip is a cut with scissors

explanation.surface: An ordinary chopped vegetable on the kitchen board.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale root crop related to the carrot, so an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Foreboding points to a man in here

indicators.note: in puts the compass letters and the name inside the word for here

parts.note: present means here, as answered at roll call
E and N are compass points, east and north
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: A bad feeling that someone's arrows are aimed at a man inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' looks like aiming but gives E and N; with TIM they go inside PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is an intuition that something, usually bad, is about to happen.

clue.text: Shakespearian father of Odysseus

definitions.meaning: a character in Shakespeare's Hamlet, Ophelia's brother, who duels with the prince
in Greek myth the king of Ithaca whose son was the wandering hero of the Odyssey

explanation.surface: A claim that some Shakespeare figure fathered the Greek hero of the Odyssey.
explanation.walkthrough: One name serves two stories: Polonius's son in Hamlet and the old king of Ithaca in Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to Polonius's son in Hamlet and to the Ithacan king in Homer's epic.

clue.text: "Fatty!" Poe said, upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe, upset, calls someone 'Fatty!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges POESAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fat store, so the word is an adjective meaning fatty.

clue.text: "Some think him ill-tempered and -"(Lear)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Edward Lear's comic self-portrait poem How Pleasant to Know Mr Lear, whose line ends on a word for odd

explanation.surface: A line of verse by Edward Lear with its final word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear, the Victorian nonsense poet, wrote of himself 'Some think him ill-tempered and queer'; the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme word completing Lear's line, used in its old sense of odd or eccentric.

clue.text: Give new order to cultivate stretch of open country

parts.note: to rear is to raise or grow, as crops or animals
a range is a wide area of open grazing land

explanation.surface: Instructions to farm a stretch of open land in a new pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things into a different sequence or arrangement is to give them a new order.

clue.text: Kind of law stunt Rita spoilt

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rita has spoilt a stunt involving some kind of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' rearranges STUNTRITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws that break up monopolies are a kind of legislation in America.

clue.text: Explain poor reprint to film character

indicators.note: a poor reprint is a badly made one, so the letters of reprint are jumbled

parts.note: E.T. is the alien in Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: Someone must account for a shoddy reprint of a film character's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges REPRINT into INTERPR, and ET, Spielberg's alien, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to make its meaning clear, a synonym of explain.

clue.text: This bar's in suspension

parts.note: a car's suspension often uses a bar that resists twisting, named after that twisting force

explanation.surface: A bar is closed down for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' and 'suspension' suggest a pub temporarily shut, but this is car engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar that springs back when twisted is fitted in a vehicle's suspension.

clue.text: Loner who acts like dissatisfied compiler, one might almost say

indicators.note: almost say means the clue phrase gives something close in sound, not an exact match

parts.note: a setter unhappy with a puzzle writes the clues again

explanation.surface: A solitary person behaves like a crossword setter unhappy with the work.
explanation.walkthrough: A compiler who dislikes their clues re-clues them; 're-clues' said aloud is close to the answer, hence 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit avoids society, a solitary person who keeps away from others.

clue.text: Church articles contain this for guidance

indicators.note: the two words contain the answer in their letters, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Church articles are said to hold something meant to guide the faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the words: churCH ARTicles. 'Church' looks like it gives CH alone, but it lends only its last two letters to the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator's map is used to guide a ship, so the answer is something for guidance.

clue.text: Limit swindle with punishment

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a fine is a money penalty

explanation.surface: A call to restrict fraud with penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict something within bounds is to limit it.

clue.text: Where one lands in song and wine (but no women)

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Song and wine but no women, a twist on the old saying about pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket plays on 'wine, women and song' and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes touch down at an aerodrome, the place where a flight lands.

clue.text: Foolish time to start bed for fruit

indicators.note: to start says this piece comes first, before the word for bed

parts.note: the first of April, April Fool's Day, written short as APR plus I for one
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A silly moment to begin planting a bed of fruit trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The foolish time is April 1st, APR I, which comes 'to start' before COT, a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-yellow stone fruit, so an example of fruit.

clue.text: Article has a jolly warmth

parts.note: the is the definite article
jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Something has a cheerful warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like cheerful, but it is old slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat used in gas billing, so a measure of warmth.

clue.text: Paddy's Tyrone's first worker odd!

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the name Tyrone

parts.note: a worker ant is the standard crossword worker
rum is an old British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Some Irishman called Paddy finds an odd worker from County Tyrone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irish name, given Tyrone (a county in Northern Ireland), but it means a fit of temper. RUM is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British slang for a fit of rage, the same as a sudden outburst of temper.

clue.text: Long work you're to hear as a connoisseur

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem or film

indicators.note: to hear says the word is taken as it sounds, not as it is spelt

parts.note: you're said aloud gives the sound of the ending -ure

explanation.surface: A long book you must listen to in order to count as a person of taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hear' gives the sound of YOU'RE, written URE, after EPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with refined taste in food and wine is a connoisseur of the table.

clue.text: Old beast, a French one with hoof trouble

parts.note: un is French for a
I is the Roman numeral for one
a corn is a painful patch on a foot, and horses can get them in the hoof

explanation.surface: An old horse with a French owner has foot problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A horned horse of legend, so a beast of old myth.

clue.text: When not on holiday it takes wine — but not all the time

parts.note: in term, at school or college, is when the holidays are over
taken as written
tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Away from holidays someone drinks wine, though only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TERM is school time, not the holidays. TENT is a deep red wine from Spain, mostly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occurring on and off happens only at intervals, never continuously.
